title: Cross-org audit access returns 403 not 404, creating an ID-enumeration side channel
description: findAudit() returns 404 'Intelligent audit not found' (intelligent-audit.controller.js:128-134) only when the ID doesn't exist at all; assertOrgAccess() returns 403 'Access denied' (:115-119) when the ID exists but belongs to another org. An attacker can distinguish 'exists in another tenant' from 'does not exist' by comparing status codes.
preconditions: Org A and Org B each have at least one IntelligentAudit document
Valid JWT for a user in Org A
steps: As an Org A user, call GET /api/intelligent-audit/:auditId with a real auditId belonging to Org B
As the same user, call GET /api/intelligent-audit/:auditId with a well-formed but nonexistent ObjectId
expectedResult: First call returns 403 'Access denied'; second call returns 404 'Intelligent audit not found'. No audit content from Org B is returned in either case, but the status-code difference should be flagged as an enumeration risk for remediation (consider returning 404 uniformly for cross-tenant IDs).

title: PATCH /:auditId/phase/:phaseNumber spreads req.body unvalidated into phaseStatus, bypassing every phase-completion guard
description: updatePhaseStatus (intelligent-audit.controller.js:946-962) runs `audit.phaseStatus[key] = { ...existing, ...req.body }` with no field whitelist, gated only by permission 'audit.update' (not an admin-only action). A caller can force isCompleted/isActive flags directly, skipping IA_GAP_ANALYSIS_LOCKED, the Phase-3-completed guard, and the zero-controls-selected guard entirely.
preconditions: Logged in as a user who holds only 'audit.update' (not an admin role)
Audit is in Phase 4 with unresolved gaps and gap analysis never run
steps: Call PATCH /api/intelligent-audit/:auditId/phase/4 with body {"isCompleted": true, "isActive": false}
expectedResult: Current behavior: the PATCH succeeds and phaseStatus.phase4.isCompleted becomes true with no gap analysis ever having run and no gaps resolved — demonstrating a phase can be marked complete by directly injecting fields via req.body. This should be flagged as a P0 remediation item: whitelist the fields updatePhaseStatus accepts per phase.

title: GET /my-assignments has no organizationId filter and can leak another org's assignment data to a multi-org user
description: getMyAssignments' four aggregation builders (buildStrategicQuery:5179, buildTacticalQuery:5273, buildCustomWorkflowQuery:5383, buildRemediationQuery:5470) filter only by assignedTo — unlike every other handler in the module, none of them add an organizationId: req.orgId match stage.
preconditions: A ClientUser is (or was previously) assigned a question/gap in Org A
The same user is currently authenticated in an Org B session (multi-org membership)
steps: As the user, with an active Org B session/orgId context, call GET /api/intelligent-audit/my-assignments
expectedResult: Current behavior: the Org A assignment (with its auditTitle, frameworkName, controlTitle, questionText) is returned even though the caller's session orgId is Org B — a cross-tenant data leak. Expected fix: add organizationId: req.orgId to all four aggregation builders so only current-org assignments are returned.

title: Evidence-existence probe via attachEvidenceToControl fires before the audit's org ownership is checked
description: attachEvidenceToControl/bulkAttachEvidenceToControl (intelligent-audit.controller.js:2374-2380, 2418-2426) validate that the Evidence document exists globally (AppError.notFound('Evidence not found')) before calling assertOrgAccess on the audit. A caller can supply an arbitrary/invalid auditId and still learn whether a given evidenceId exists anywhere on the platform.
preconditions: Caller has a valid JWT but no legitimate access to the target auditId
steps: Call POST /api/intelligent-audit/:bogusAuditId/phase/3/control/0/evidence with an evidenceId known to exist in another org
Call the same endpoint with an evidenceId known not to exist at all
expectedResult: Current behavior: both calls return the Evidence-existence check result (404 'Evidence not found' only for the second) before any audit-ownership error would fire, letting an attacker enumerate evidenceId existence platform-wide independent of audit access. Should be flagged for remediation: check audit/org ownership before evidence existence.

title: linkEvidenceToAttachment accepts an arbitrary unvalidated string as evidenceId, unlike attachEvidenceToControl
description: linkEvidenceToAttachment (intelligent-audit.controller.js:3025-3038) explicitly documents accepting a non-ObjectId custom string (e.g. 'EV-xxx') and persists it into entry.evidenceId with no format or existence validation at all — an inconsistency versus attachEvidenceToControl, which requires a real Evidence document to exist first.
preconditions: Logged in as a user with audit.update on a real audit/control
steps: Call the evidence-attachment-workflow endpoint for a Phase 3 control with evidenceId set to an arbitrary garbage string (e.g. '<script>alert(1)</script>' or a long random string)
Fetch the control's evidence-attachment record afterward
expectedResult: Current behavior: the arbitrary string is accepted and stored verbatim in entry.evidenceId with no validation or existence check — confirm this does not enable stored XSS when rendered in the UI, and flag the inconsistency with the stricter attachEvidenceToControl path for remediation.

title: Framework audit search parameter safely escapes regex metacharacters instead of being interpreted as a live regex
description: getIntelligentAuditsByFramework (intelligent-audit.controller.js:882-889) escapes the search string with esc = search.trim().replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&') before building the $regex query — a positive control confirming no regex-injection/ReDoS surface on this endpoint.
preconditions: At least 2 audits exist for the framework with titles 'Audit One' and 'AuditXOne'
expectedResult: The literal dot in 'Audit.One' is NOT treated as a regex wildcard — only an audit literally titled 'Audit.One' matches (not 'AuditXOne'). The ReDoS-shaped pattern '(a+)+$' returns quickly (no catastrophic backtracking) and matches nothing or is treated as a literal string.

title: Deleting evidence/policy/vendor links or removing a participant only requires audit.update, not audit.delete
description: Despite being DELETE HTTP verbs, removeEvidenceFromControl, unlinkPolicyFromControl, unlinkVendorFromControl, and removeAuditParticipant (intelligent-audit.routes.js lines 88,97,99,144) all require only 'audit.update'. A user granted update-but-not-delete permission can still perform destructive unlink/remove operations.
preconditions: A test role is granted 'audit.update' but explicitly NOT 'audit.delete'
steps: As the audit.update-only user, call DELETE /api/intelligent-audit/:auditId/phase/3/control/:controlIndex/evidence/:evidenceId
As the same user, call DELETE /api/intelligent-audit/:auditId/participants/:userId
expectedResult: Both DELETE calls currently succeed for a user who lacks 'audit.delete', confirming the permission model treats these as updates rather than deletions. Flag for a product/security decision on whether 'audit.delete' should gate these destructive sub-resource removals.

title: addControlToPhase2 (a scope-expanding POST) is gated by audit.update, not audit.create
description: intelligent-audit.routes.js:67 requires only 'audit.update' for POST /:auditId/phase/2/controls, whereas the module's only other resource-creation-shaped POSTs (createIntelligentAudit, createCustomQuestion) require 'audit.create'. A role holding audit.update but not audit.create can still add new controls to an audit's scope.
preconditions: A test role is granted 'audit.update' but explicitly NOT 'audit.create'
steps: As the audit.update-only user, call POST /api/intelligent-audit/:auditId/phase/2/controls with a valid requirementId from the audit's own framework
expectedResult: The control is added successfully (200/201) despite the caller lacking 'audit.create' — confirm this is intended (scope editing treated as an update) or flag for permission-model alignment.

title: Frontend hides Intelli Audit actions but the corresponding API endpoints must independently reject unauthorized calls
description: All Intelli Audit pages use PermissionGate (permission='pre_audit.read') and PermissionHide (permission='audit.update'/'audit.create') to hide UI, per PermissionGate.jsx's OR-based project-grant logic. UI hiding is not a substitute for server-side enforcement — this case verifies the API rejects direct calls from a user who only fails the permission check.
preconditions: A user has no 'audit.create' permission (globally or project-scoped)
steps: Confirm the 'Start New Audit' button is not rendered for this user in the UI
Directly call POST /api/intelligent-audit with a valid title/description/frameworkId/projectId using this user's JWT
expectedResult: The direct API call is rejected with 403 (permission-middleware error), independent of and consistent with the UI's hidden button — confirming the client-side hide is backed by real server-side authorization, not merely cosmetic.
